subject: health
title: Mastery check: coping and regulation strategies
essentialQuestion: How can I manage strong feelings and know when to reach for support?
materials: cards or paper for a coping toolkit
optional timer for a calming practice
keyPoints: Slow breathing with a longer out-breath lowers the body's alarm response.
Grounding by naming what you can see, hear, and touch brings attention back to the present.
Movement, water, daylight, and sleep are underrated regulators.
Match the strategy to the setting — some work in a classroom, some only at home.
Strategies work better when practised before you need them.
privacySafeScenario: Build a toolkit for someone who gets overwhelmed in noisy places and cannot leave the room. What actually fits that constraint?
studentTask: The learner applies what they learned about coping and regulation strategies to a new fictional situation and records the choice plus the reason behind it.
knowledgeCheck: Explain coping and regulation strategies to someone who has not learned it yet, using one example.
completionCriteria: The learner completes the central task about coping and regulation strategies.
The learner gives a reason, an example, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name one next step.
adaptationChoices: Coping strategies may be movement-based, still, sensory, verbal, or silent, and each learner selects strategies their body and setting allow. Scenario responses may be pointed to, chosen from options, drawn, spoken, or written.
extensionChallenge: Apply what you learned about coping and regulation strategies under a new constraint, compare two reasonable approaches, or teach the idea to a family member with an original fictional example.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, signed, drawn, or pointed responses; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
trustedAdultNote: Direct urgent safety, health, or mental-health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.

optionalReflection.prompt: With a guardian, agree one signal you can use at home that means "I need a few minutes". This is optional. No purchase, account creation, photograph, measurement, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
